AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's pool-wide verdict, copied not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation IS construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect (13 Block via CreatureCmd.GainBlock(..., ValueProp.Move) and ArtifactPower 1, CubexConstruct.cs:87-94) is applied from `__init__` (cubex_construct.py:29-32). The game applies it from MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom (MonsterModel.cs:313-316 is a no-op base, so the override is the whole effect), awaited by CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded inside StartCombatInternal, i.e. after every creature is on the board and before Hook.BeforeCombatStart. Same observable today on all three clauses SHARED-FINDINGS establishes by execution: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the reachable hooks (relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38, relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53, relics/vambrace.py:55-73, relics/paels_legion.py:36-43) all gate on the player and a monster's starting power/block is self-applied with no card; (b) HP-roll inversion -- of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp and only inside revive() (powers.py:2063-2067), never at apply time; (c) roll ordering -- all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-ops (monster_probes.py roll-order). This unit exercises the BLOCK half of the shared verdict, whose clause (a) listeners are relics/vambrace.py:55-73 and relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 on modify_block_multiplicative -- both gate on the player. The override's remaining two statements are the `Creature.CurrentHpChanged += OnHpChanged` subscription (an sfx parameter, CubexConstruct.cs:102-108) and `IsBurrowed = true` (an animator predicate), neither mechanical. Rule 7: the four relic files and sts2_rl/powers.py named above are NOT hashed by this record (powers.py is hashed only where this record cites it with line numbers).

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Hand-rolled port of CubexConstruct.cs:110-126. The C# graph is a pure chain CHARGE_UP_MOVE -> REPEATER_BLAST_MOVE -> REPEATER_BLAST_MOVE_2 -> EXPEL_MOVE -> REPEATER_BLAST_MOVE (back to the FIRST blast, not to CHARGE_UP). The two blast nodes are distinct ids sharing one delegate and one intent, so the port collapses them into a single 'RB' key and counts position with _cycle_step -- the emitted sequence is what matters. Executed, not asserted (verdict rule 5): `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py chain` rebuilds the C# GenerateMoveStateMachine graph node for node on the sim's OWN MonsterMoveStateMachine primitives (so the walk, the repeat rules and the single-NextFloat(total) draw are the audited machinery) and diffs it against the shipped port over 20 turns from an identically seeded RunRngSet. (the reference's REPEATER_BLAST_MOVE_2 is folded to REPEATER_BLAST_MOVE for the diff, which is exactly the collapse being checked). Result: 20/20 turns identical -- CHARGE, RB, RB, EXPEL, RB, RB, EXPEL, ... -- and 0 MonsterAi draws on both sides.

CubexConstruct.cs:45 (DeadlyEnemies, 8, 7) -> 7 = _RB_DMG; :47 (6, 5) -> 5 = _EXPEL_DMG; ExpelBlastMove is `.WithHitCount(2)` (:155) = _EXPEL_HITS; ChargeUpMove and RepeaterBlastMove each apply StrengthPower 2m (:135, :147) = _CHARGE_STR/_RB_STR; GainBlock 13m (:90) = _START_BLOCK (cubex_construct.py:14-19). guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:422-442, `_roll_parity_hp`), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit's MaxInitialHp is `=> MinInitialHp`, so the range is the single value 65 and no endpoint can be lost; the check is recorded anyway because an off-by-one would turn a one-element candidate list into an empty one and change which ARM of SetUniqueMonsterHpValue runs (NextItem vs NextInt), which is a stream-position difference even when the HP is identical. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [65,65], observed [65,65], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 65 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:236) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
